clue.text: Moody relief worker crazy about date

blocks.note: a temp is a temporary worker who relieves or covers for staff
a date in the sense of a period of history
informal word for mad

explanation.surface: A sulky stand-in worker gets worked up over a romantic date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' only places the date beside the crazy part, as in 'round about'; nothing is wrapped. 'Date' means a period of history, not a romantic outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone temperamental has unpredictable mood swings, a direct synonym of moody.

clue.text: Jerusalem men, thalidomide victims, wanted a bit of cheese

indicators.note: only a bit of the run of words is wanted, so the answer sits inside them

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third
surface padding to complete the picture

explanation.surface: A grim picture of men in Jerusalem affected by a drug, craving some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmenthal is a Swiss hard cheese with large holes, an example of the category named.

clue.text: One finds four suits in these and gets ready to go away

definitions.text: One finds four suits in these

blocks.clueFragment: One finds four suits in these
blocks.note: first meaning: decks of playing cards, each holding hearts, clubs, diamonds and spades
second meaning: fills a suitcase before a trip

explanation.surface: A traveller loads several suits into luggage before setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: The suits look like clothing for a trip, but the first meaning is about card suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Card decks are called packs in Britain, and a person who packs prepares luggage for departure.

clue.text: Cuts down coloured cues for playing with

indicators.note: things picked up for playing with get moved about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: red is a colour
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shortens snooker cues painted bright colours so they can play with them.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce something is to lessen or cut it down, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Gangster's girlfriend you and I caught with an invertebrate

blocks.note: a moll is a gangster's female companion
the pronoun for the speaker plus another
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: We nab a mobster's girlfriend along with a spineless accomplice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invertebrate' reads as an insult for a coward, but it is the zoological definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Molluscs such as snails and squid have no backbone, so they are an example of invertebrates.

clue.text: Deny going round back to one looking for bargain

indicators.note: going back means the short word is read from right to left
the word for deny encircles the other letters, going round them

blocks.note: to negate is to deny
taken as written
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone turns down an offer and comes back, hunting for a good deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bargain' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb: to haggle.
explanation.definitionFit: To bargain is to haggle over terms, which is exactly what it means to negotiate.

clue.text: Capone takes a moment to see where Davy Crockett died

blocks.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster
taken as written
mo is informal for a moment, as in 'half a mo'

explanation.surface: A gangster pauses briefly to visit a famous historic battle site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half a mo' is British slang for a short moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The frontiersman Davy Crockett was killed defending the Texas mission at the 1836 siege of the Alamo.

clue.text: Titles for excellent vessels

blocks.note: champion as an informal adjective meaning first-rate
ships are seagoing vessels

explanation.surface: A shipping firm awards honours to its finest boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion!' is a northern English exclamation meaning splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Titles in sport are the championships won, such as world or league crowns.

clue.text: Remembers unit arranging repayment

indicators.note: arranging puts items into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An office department recalls setting up a scheme to pay people back.
explanation.definitionFit: Reimbursement is money paid back to cover an expense, a direct synonym of repayment.

clue.text: Sort of maniac likely to make someone late?

definitions.text: Sort of maniac likely to make someone late?

blocks.clueFragment: Sort of maniac likely to make someone late?
blocks.note: surface reading: a disorganised person who keeps others waiting
setter's reading: 'the late' means dead, so this maniac kills

explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' looks like 'not on time', but it is the late in 'the late Mr Smith': deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: A maniac who kills people is a murderous one, the adjective describing killing a person.

clue.text: She's given ¿1,000 to run

blocks.note: £1,000 is a grand, abbreviated G; the ¿ is a garbled pound sign
to race is to run fast

explanation.surface: A woman receives a thousand pounds to take part in a sponsored run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' stands for a woman's name; G for grand is standard slang for a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace is a common female first name, so a woman can be referred to by it.

clue.text: Diminished by getting married in America

blocks.note: M is the standard abbreviation for married
taken as written
the United States

explanation.surface: Someone feels reduced by having wed in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it places one piece inside another, but here it is simply part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Minus as an adjective describes a quantity that has been reduced or taken away from, so less.

clue.text: Royal household will need space for cases here

blocks.note: a monarch's court is the royal household
room in the sense of available space

explanation.surface: The royal family needs more storage space for their luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' look like suitcases, but they are legal cases heard before a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal trials are heard in this chamber, so the place where cases are tried describes it.

clue.text: In this place a pole remains firm in something

blocks.note: in here means in this place
S, south, is one of the two poles

explanation.surface: Here a post stands solidly fixed in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A quality that inheres in something is permanently fixed within it as an essential part.

clue.text: Repeat again and again: soldiers get irate about Lawrence

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the angry word is split around the other

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
taken as written
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: Troops grow angry about Lawrence of Arabia and say so over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: No anagram here: the angry word just opens after its first letter. The Royal Engineers are a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To reiterate is to say something once more, often repeatedly, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Union leader after two teas at a French country house

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter is wanted
after sends the union letter to follow the tea pieces rather than precede them

blocks.note: cha is slang for tea, followed by tea itself
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A trade union boss takes afternoon tea twice at a grand house in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha (or char) is old British slang for tea, from Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: A château is a large country mansion or castle in France.

clue.text: Leave it on when changing height

indicators.note: changing means altering the order, so the letters come out rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to keep something switched on while adjusting its altitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevation is the height of a place above sea level, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Turn fully in to render ineffective

indicators.note: to turn something over is to reshape it, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to switch something completely off.
explanation.definitionFit: To nullify a law or contract is to cancel its force, making it void and without effect.

clue.text: Becomes jaundiced; with a cry of pain shouts about it

indicators.note: the shouting word goes about the cry, wrapping round it

blocks.note: to yell is to shout
the exclamation when hurt

explanation.surface: A patient turning sickly cries out in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' points back to the cry of pain: the shouts go round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaundice turns the skin a yellow colour, so to become jaundiced is to turn that hue.

clue.text: Old policeman the French noblemen must go round to see

definitions.note: singular, while the answer is plural

indicators.note: the nobles go round, enclosing the French article

blocks.note: peers are members of the nobility
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Nobles have to make a visit to a retired constable.
explanation.walkthrough: Peeler is old British slang for a police officer, after Sir Robert Peel who founded the Metropolitan Police; the clue's singular definition slightly mismatches the plural answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Early London constables were nicknamed after their founder, Robert Peel, hence the historical slang term.

clue.text: Upstart found the normal meeting place pointless

indicators.note: without its point, the venue loses the letter that stands for a compass point

blocks.note: par is the normal or average standard
a venue is where people meet

explanation.surface: A social climber thought the usual gathering spot was a waste of time.
explanation.walkthrough: E for east is the compass point dropped from VENUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is someone newly risen to wealth or status who lacks social polish, as is an upstart.

clue.text: Person in YHA wants Head Office to sack first cashier

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
the opening letter of the word
a bank teller handles cash

explanation.surface: A youth hostel guest wants headquarters to fire the leading cashier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack first' reads as dismissing someone, but it only supplies a letter. The YHA is the Youth Hostels Association in England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A hosteller is someone who stays at youth hostels, as members of the Youth Hostels Association do.

clue.text: Mark is wrong about the Territorial Army

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the wrong word goes around the army

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong
the TA is Britain's part-time volunteer army reserve

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark is mistaken about the reserve forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name, but it is the noun for a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain is a discoloured spot or blemish, a kind of mark left on fabric.

clue.text: Hives finally heat lots of bees

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the closing letter
to heat is to warm

explanation.surface: Beehives eventually warm up with crowds of bees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hives' looks like part of the bee picture, but it only gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large group of bees leaving a hive together with a queen.

clue.text: Sordid joint by the end of the day

indicators.note: the end of a word is its closing letter only

blocks.note: a seam is the joint where two pieces meet
the closing letter

explanation.surface: A disreputable pub visited late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a dive bar or cannabis, but it is a seam.
explanation.definitionFit: The seamy side of life is its squalid, unpleasant part, so seamy is a synonym of sordid.

clue.text: Silly chump Lazarus found hiding in a Spanish square

indicators.note: something hiding in the words is concealed inside them, across a gap

blocks.note: surface padding describing the chump
the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A foolish man named Lazarus lurks in a town square in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' only colours the surface; the answer runs across the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaza is the Spanish word for a public square in a town.

clue.text: A job to be done in the theatre?

definitions.note: a phrase for what happens there, not a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: a task or undertaking
second meaning: surgery performed in a hospital operating theatre

explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests a stage, but the question mark points to the operating theatre in a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertaking or task can be called an operation, and so can the surgery a surgeon performs.

clue.text: Preparing to take part, if someone else is ill

definitions.text: Preparing to take part, if someone else is ill

blocks.note: surface reading: getting ready to join in something
setter's reading: 'part' is a stage role, learned by an actor who covers when the lead is off sick

explanation.walkthrough: 'Take part' sounds like joining in, but a part here is a role in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who learns a lead's role to stand in during illness is doing the work of a theatrical stand-in.
